ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-closing screening of all general partners, limited partners, ultimate beneficial owners, attorneys, and senior officers against: (i) Global Affairs Canada's Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List under the Special Economic Measures Act; (ii) the Criminal Code terrorist entity list and United Nations Security Council consolidated list; (iii) the U.S. Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list and sectoral sanctions; and (iv) domestic and foreign PEP databases (politically exposed persons, heads of international organizations, and close associates/family members). Enhanced due diligence applies where UBOs reside in or source funds from FATF high-risk or non-cooperative jurisdictions. Payment rails (Wise B2B and Payoneer) require equivalent KYC and sanctions controls in their merchant bank flows.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Registry Services – BC Corporate Online (bcregistry.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory name clearance is administered by the Registrar of Companies under the Business Corporations Act and the Partnership Act. Permitted names may be expressed in English or French using the Roman alphabet; non-Roman script names must be transliterated into Roman characters. The legal element of a limited partnership name generally requires the words 'Limited Partnership', 'L.P.', 'Société en commandite', or 'S.E.C.', and must be set out at the end of the name. The selected name must be distinguishable from all existing corporate, partnership, trade marks and protected names in British Columbia, and may not suggest a form of entity other than a limited partnership.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is refused, the application can re-view the reasons via the BC Registry name rejection search console. The applicant may submit a request for reconsideration to the Registrar of Companies within 30 calendar days, accompanied by a new name request, a written legal submission, evidence of trade-mark registration, business name usage or common law reputation, and any required consent or exemption documents. If the Registrar upholds the rejection, the applicant may file a petition for judicial review in the Supreme Court of British Columbia within 60 days of the final administrative refusal. A new reservation can also be filed immediately with an amended name variant. Legal counsel should evaluate appeal cost-benefit against preparing an alternate name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible for the BC registered records office provided the provider supplies a physical street address within British Columbia and the arrangement is not merely a post-office box. The BC Registry will accept a registered agent's street address and service-of-process arrangement. For Canada Revenue Agency and cross-border substance purposes, however, the CRA may disregard a purely nominal presence, so the partnership should maintain substantive evidence of actual management and business activity in BC if it seeks to benefit from domestic tax classification or treaty access; an app-store optimization and multilingual search agency can satisfy commercial substance requirements through active employees, contracts, bank accounts, and marketing IP management in BC.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (approximately 5% annual) for a standard-risk, non-licensed digital service entity. FINTRAC and Canada Revenue Agency examinations are typically desk-based, but unannounced physical inspections may occur where non-arm's-length payments, excessive input tax credits, loss histories, or GST/PST registration anomalies give rise to higher tax or anti-money-laundering risk.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Partnership Act, RSBC 1996, c. 348, Part 3 (Limited Partnerships), ss. 44 et seq.; Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c. 57 (for a corporate general partner acting as manager)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BC Registries and Online Services, Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statement of Registration of Limited Partnership (Form LP 1)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital required under the BC Partnership Act; the parties' capital contributions are set out in the Statement of Registration, and no escrow or deposit of the stated partnership capital is mandated prior to registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the corporate general partner of [Name] Limited Partnership, acting by its board of directors, hereby: (1) approves the capital contributions of the limited and general partners as set forth in the Statement of Registration of Limited Partnership; (2) adopts the registered office located in British Columbia and appoints the registered office representative; (3) appoints the chief compliance officer and managing representative of the partnership; (4) authorizes opening business bank accounts, engaging payment processors, and executing customer contracts; and (5) authorizes filing of the Statement of Registration and all ancillary statutory returns with BC Registries. This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services Name Request Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a Name Request application for the proposed limited partnership name in the BC Registry's online portal. The system performs a NUANS corporate name search, and upon approval the name is reserved for a statutory period. If a non-Canadian general partner is identified, the application and supporting identification must be notarized before submission.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, file a revised Name Request with one or more new distinctive elements within the reserved statutory window; if the 90-day reservation lapses, restart the name search and resolve any conflicts with the Corporate Registry counsel.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and Execute Statement of Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form LP 1 'Statement of Registration of Limited Partnership' with the full partnership name, BC registered office address, mailing address, full legal names and addresses of all general partners, and the names of all limited partners. The form must be executed by every general partner and, where a general partner is a body corporate, by its authorized officer; all non-Canadian execution pages must be notarized.
required_dossiers: Form LP 1 Statement of Registration of Limited Partnership
Consent to act as general partner
Certificate of corporate general partner existence
Notarized resolutions for foreign corporate general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any identified deficiencies on Form LP 1 and re-file; if the registry questions any field, submit an amended Statement of Registration with supporting evidence of good standing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit Registration and Pay Filing Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the BC Registries online portal using a BCeID account, upload the executed Form LP 1 and all required dossiers, pay the applicable filing fee using a credit card or direct bank transfer, and retain the system-generated acknowledgement of registration as evidence of partnership formation.
required_dossiers: Notarized identification of each general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, respond to the registry through the online portal within the stated deadline with corrected schedules; if the filing is rejected, resubmit after curing the deficiency without incurring a new name search unless the name reservation lapsed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establish Registered Office and Statutory Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services (Registered Office Filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notice of registered office address in British Columbia and confirm the registered office representative within the statutory period after registration. Physical presence at the registered office is not required solely for a registered office if a qualified representative is appointed; maintain the partnership register, accounting records, and statutory minute book at an accessible location in British Columbia.
required_dossiers: Notice of address of registered office
Consent to act as registered office representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry requires a physical inspection or rejects the office address, file an amended Statement of Registration designating a compliant BC street address and submit the revised consent within the registry's query period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City of Vancouver Business Licence Office (or applicable BC municipal revenue division)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a current business licence in the municipality where the SEO administrative office is physically located. Submit the business licence application with the limited partnership registration certificate, lease or ownership evidence, and partnership details. Confirm that the zoning of the premises permits general office and professional agency use, and display the licence at the place of business.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If zoning or use constitutes a non-conformity, apply to the municipal planning department for a discretionary use approval or a variance; alternatively, relocate to an office address that is compliant and file a revised Notice of Registered Office with BC Registries.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and BC Ministry of Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Canada Revenue Agency Form RC1 to obtain a business number, GST/HST account, and any payroll account for the limited partnership. Register with the BC Ministry of Finance for employer health tax and applicable BC provincial sales tax (PST) where services are exempt or taxable according to the exemption certificate regime. Also update the beneficial ownership information of the general and limited partners in the BC registry if any statutory register so requires.
required_dossiers: Statement of Registration of Limited Partnership
General partner personal identification for beneficial ownership reporting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA or BC Ministry queries an account, provide the complete partnership agreement and a certified copy of the general partner's authorization, and correct any stated fiscal periods or partner allocations within the CRA's prescribed response window.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - no sector-specific industrial licensing board for NAICS 541810 (Advertising Agencies) in British Columbia; only general municipal business licensing applies.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: British Columbia Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - the proposed office-based digital services operation does not trigger the Environmental Assessment Act and involves no industrial activity; no formal EIA report or registration required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater, VOC, or hazardous air emissions are generated by office and data-processing activities. The operation must comply with local municipal solid waste and e-waste recycling bylaws, and any electronic equipment disposal must follow the BC Recycling Regulation (Electronic Products).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain a local fire safety inspection and building occupancy certificate for the leased office space; comply with WorkSafeBC occupational health and safety clearance, including ergonomics, electrical safety, and emergency evacuation standards under the Workers Compensation Act and the Occupational Health and Safety Regulation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), in coordination with the Department of Finance Canada and the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI), with FINTRAC administering cross-border financial reporting obligations under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is freely convertible and floats under a market-determined exchange rate regime with no direct central bank intervention framework for routine corporate flows. Canada imposes no exchange controls on current-account or capital-account transactions; non-residents may invest in, fund, and repatriate from a British Columbia limited partnership without foreign-exchange authorization. Profit allocations to non-resident limited partners are taxed under Part I of the Income Tax Act on the Canadian-source business income; passive payments such as interest, royalties, and management fees are subject to Part XIII withholding at 25% unless reduced by tax treaty (e.g., Canada-US Convention: arm's-length interest generally 0%, royalties 10%).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory surrender timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no required repatriation of export or cross-border service receipts. The ISIC 7310 ASO/SEO/localization agency may retain earned fees in CAD or foreign currency accounts. Practical compliance obligations include FINTRAC electronic funds transfer reporting for cross-border transactions of CAD 10,000 or more, six-year record retention of invoices and contracts, and CRA Form T106 information returns for payments to non-residents.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: High as supplementary settlement rails; Medium as the sole banking relationship. Wise (Wise Payments Canada Ltd.) and Payoneer (Payoneer Canada ULC) are FINTRAC-registered money services businesses under the PCMLTFA and hold British Columbia Money Services Business licenses; both can settle inbound international client receipts and make outbound contractor payments in multiple currencies. Legal constraints: these EMIs cannot offer CDIC-insured CAD deposits, cheque clearing, credit facilities, or commercial standby letters of credit; they are operationally suitable for low-value, high-volume app-platform payouts but should be configured to sweep funds automatically to a primary Schedule I bank account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under PCMLTFA identity rules, at least one authorized signatory (generally the general partner's principal) must complete identity verification. Physical branch attendance is the operational default for most Schedule I commercial onboarding, but remote opening is permissible where the bank applies the video/dual-process method or accepts certified true copies of passport and proof of address notarized by a lawyer or notary in the signatory's jurisdiction. Directors of a non-resident general partner generally need not travel to Canada if a Canadian-resident authorized signatory is appointed and the bank's commercial AML officer approves remote KYC; a notarized LP Agreement, BC Form LP registration, CRA business number, and a banker's reference from the partner's home institution are required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: LP structure with a non-resident or zero-tax-jurisdiction general partner and opaque ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide BC Form LP registration and Annual Report; registered office lease; notarized LP Agreement and general partner board resolutions listing all UBOs with passport copies and residential addresses; CRA business number confirmation; CRS self-certification (CRA RC518) and W-8BEN-E/W-8BEN for non-resident partners; banker's reference letter from the general partner's home institution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent small inbound cross-border wires from overseas app developers/platforms with inconsistent remitter names.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide executed Master Services Agreements and statements of work for ASO/SEO/localization services; invoice-to-wire reconciliation ledger; accounting-system payment matching report; revenue recognition policy; a concise business narrative describing the low-risk digital marketing model and confirming the absence of unrelated third-party payments or cash pass-through arrangements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Periodic draws to non-resident partners, or outbound payments characterized as management fees or royalties without evidentiary substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide partnership capital account ledger showing contributed capital and cumulative draws; general partner minutes authorizing distributions; filed T5013 partnership information return and any required T106/NR4 forms; on management fees, provide an executed fee agreement, fee invoices, an arm's-length reasonableness analysis, and evidence of Part XIII withholding remittance or an approved NR301 treaty reduction application.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Foreign investors wire funds via SWIFT MT103/gpi to the LP's Schedule I bank account using purpose code CAPT (capital contribution); field 70 must state: 'Contribution to limited partnership capital per LP Agreement dated [date]; no services in exchange; source: [investor]; CRS TIN: [identifier].' The bank will verify the investor's identity and source of funds and may require the executed subscription agreement, capital account statement, and a current CRS self-certification. No central bank approval or CAD conversion is required; contributed funds may remain in USD or be converted at the bank's prevailing spot or forward rate.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail is SWIFT MT103/gpi through the LP's Schedule I bank, with same-day CAD interbank clearing via Payments Canada LVTS and USD clearing through the bank's United States correspondent (e.g., TD Bank, N.A. or BMO Harris Bank, N.A.). Contractor and vendor payments for translation/localization and SEO services should reference invoice numbers in MT103 field 70; Canadian-dollar domestic disbursements may use direct deposit via Automated Funds Transfer or LVTS. Commercial letters of credit are unnecessary for the low-risk ISIC 7310 service model; a standby letter of credit may be issued for large enterprise app clients against a cash margin or committed FX/credit facility.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: OTC deliverable forward FX contracts (CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, CAD/GBP) under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and 1998 FX Definitions, maturities up to 24 months, with a committed zero-collateral FX line where available
Cross-currency vanilla FX swaps (CAD/USD) to manage timing gaps between USD receivables and CAD operating expenses
Vanilla FX options (out-of-the-money puts and calls on CAD) purchased from a Schedule I dealer for premium-only protection against adverse FX movement
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are legally permissible but commercially inefficient for CAD because the Canadian dollar is fully convertible and a deep onshore deliverable forward market exists

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the anniversary of the registration date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalties up to $500 CAD; failure to file within deadline may result in administrative strike-off of the Limited Partnership

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory independent audit for Limited Partnerships under British Columbia law; independent audit required only in exceptional cases such as public company status or specific partner thresholds
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) or International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as applicable

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual UBO confirmation required for Limited Partnerships in British Columbia; changes in partners or general partners must be notified to the Registrar within 15 days of occurrence

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $150 - $400 USD annually for registered office and compliance agent services in British Columbia
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: N/A - no statutory audit requirement for Limited Partnerships; voluntary audit fees typically range from $3,000 to $8,000 USD

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27.00% (federal 18.00% after provincial abatement + British Columbia provincial 9.00%, combined general corporate income tax rate for a limited partnership taxed as a corporation where applicable; active business income rate for a CCPC in BC is 11.00% combined, but the LP is a pass-through entity and rates apply at the partner level).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: British Columbia provides a reduced provincial corporate income tax rate of 9.00% for eligible BC-based businesses. Federal small business deduction (SBD) reduces the federal rate to 9.00% on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income for Canadian-controlled private corporations (CCPCs), but a Limited Partnership is generally a pass-through vehicle; partners compute their own taxes. No statutory tax holiday is available for ASO/SEO localization agencies; the Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) investment tax credit (ITC) is available for qualifying R&D activities at a rate of 15% for most taxpayers; the Interactive Digital Media Tax Credit (IDMTC) for BC provides a 17.5% refundable tax credit (35% of eligible labour expenditures via the BC Interactive Digital Media Tax Credit) for qualifying digital media activities, subject to eligibility criteria. For non-resident partners, income from carrying on business in Canada through the LP is subject to Part I tax on Canadian-source business income, and the LP must file a T5013 return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 – Partnership Information Return filed through the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) GST/HST NETFILE or approved third-party electronic filing software via the CRA My Business Account portal; under BC law, no separate BC partnership return is required because income is allocated to partners who file their own T1 or T2 returns; however, BC corporate partners must file BC Corporate Tax Return (Form T2, BC provincial schedule) through the same CRA portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T5013 return must be filed within 5 months after the partnership's fiscal year-end (for a partnership with a fiscal year ending December 31, the deadline is June 15 for non-corporate partners, but the T5013 itself must generally be filed no later than March 31 following the calendar year-end if all partners are individuals residing in Canada; for a partnership with any corporate partner, the T5013 is due within 5 months of the fiscal year-end). The T2 corporate income tax return for a corporate partner is due 6 months after its taxation year-end; for a BC provincial corporate return, the same T2 due date applies via the CRA's combined federal-provincial filing system.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 18 – Business Number (BN) and Legal Entity Identifier
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CRA-assigned 9-digit BN for the partnership, plus the LP registration number from the BC Registry (e.g., BC LP number).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident partner must provide its foreign tax identification number and country of residence; ensure the partnership's T5013 identifies the non-resident partner in Schedule 50 with the correct Canadian branch/agency information.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Date of the partnership's fiscal year-end. For an LP, the fiscal year-end must be a calendar year-end if all partners are individuals, but can be any date if all partners are corporations or if the partnership is a specified investment flow-through (SIFT) partnership; for a BC LP used as an ASO agency, a December 31 year-end is standard.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm consistency with the partner's own tax year; a non-resident corporate partner must use the same fiscal period as its own taxation year if it is a member of a partnership that has a corporate partner.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part II – Income/Loss from Business (T5013 Schedule 1)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report gross revenue from App Store Optimization, ASO consulting, SEO localization services, subscription fees, and performance-based growth fees. Deduct advertising costs, software subscriptions, contractor payments, sub-licensing fees, and operating expenses. For an LP, the net income or loss is allocated to partners according to the partnership agreement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must receive Form T5013 Supplementary (T5013SUM) and Schedule 1 showing their share of Canadian-source business income; the partnership must withhold non-resident withholding tax on any management fees or payments to non-residents that are not at arm's length, per Part XIII.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Used to report the partnership's country-by-country (CbC) or international activities if the LP or any partner is a member of a multinational group requiring CbC reporting. For an ASO localization agency with cross-border clients, identify jurisdictions where revenue is sourced and report the applicable tax treaty provisions for business income (Article 7 PE rules).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident partner, schedule 8 of T5013 is not applicable at the entity level; instead, the non-resident partner uses the treaty article for business profits to determine whether the partnership's Canadian activities create a permanent establishment in Canada. File Form T5013 as required and ensure the partner claims treaty relief on its home-country return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule 50 – Information Return for Non-Resident Members
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identifies each non-resident partner by name, address, country of residence, and share of partnership income. Must be completed by the partnership if any partner is non-resident.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident partner, the LP must report the partner's Canadian business income share; the non-resident partner is required to file a Canadian T1 or T2 return (or Part I election) to report this income and pay tax, unless exempted under a tax treaty. The partnership must also provide Form T5013SUM and, if requested, a copy of the DTA application.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: BC Corporate Tax Return – T2 Provincial Schedule (for corporate partners)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The province of BC uses the federal T2 return and a separate BC tax schedule (Form T2, BC Schedule 5 for provincial tax calculation) to impose the 9.00% BC corporate tax on a partner's allocated share of partnership income that is taxable in BC. For an LP with non-resident partners, the BC allocation is based on the partner's permanent establishment in BC; for a non-resident partner without a BC PE, no BC provincial tax is payable on the partnership income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporate partner that does not have a permanent establishment in BC is not subject to BC corporate income tax on its share of partnership income, but remains subject to federal Part I tax. If the partnership has a BC PE through the agency's office or employees, the non-resident corporate partner must file a BC T2 return and pay BC corporate tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty for T5013 is 5% of the unpaid tax/amount owing plus 1% per complete month of delay, capped at 12 months, for failure to file the return on time. If the partnership has more than CAD 10,000 of gross revenue, failure to file a T5013 by the due date incurs a penalty of CAD 100 per partner per day (minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 7,500 for all partners) for each day the return is late, plus a further penalty of CAD 100 per partner per day if required to file electronically. Late filing of the T2 by a corporate partner triggers a federal penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month (up to 12 months), plus a BC late-filing penalty of 10% of unpaid BC tax in some circumstances; daily interest on late federal taxes is levied at the prescribed CRA rate (currently 8% for 2024, compounded daily), and BC interest similarly applies. Failure to file can also lead to a gross-negligence penalty of 50% of the tax payable on understated income.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% (federal Part XIII withholding tax on deemed dividends paid by a partnership to non-resident partners; where the partnership is treated as a corporation for withholding purposes or where amounts are recharacterized as dividends from Canadian sources; dividends paid by a Canadian corporation to a non-resident are subject to 25% withholding tax under Income Tax Act (Canada) Part XIII, subject to treaty reduction). For a Limited Partnership that is not a corporation, distributions to non-resident partners are typically partnership distributions characterized as business income or capital gains, not dividends; however, if the LP is a "SIFT" trust or corporation-like partnership (e.g., a publicly-listed limited partnership), certain distributions are treated as dividends and subject to withholding tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief under the Canada–United States Tax Convention (or any applicable DTA), the non-resident partner must provide a Form NR301 (Declaration of Eligibility for Relief Under a Tax Convention), for the partnership to reduce Part XIII withholding on distributions or for the non-resident to claim an exemption from Canadian tax on business income absent a PE. The CRA requires a valid Certificate of Residence (Form NR301 or TRC issued by the treaty partner's tax authority) to be submitted before the payment is made. For treaty-exempt business income under Article 7 of a DTA, the non-resident partner files a Canadian tax return (T1 or T2) with a copy of the treaty article and a completed NR301 to claim exemption from Canadian tax. For Part XIII withholding on dividends/royalties/interest, the withholding agent (the LP or the paying Canadian corporation) must retain the TRC and a completed NR301 or NR302. The Canada Revenue Agency's administrative protocol requires the TRC to be submitted before the reduced rate is applied; if the TRC is unavailable, withhold at 25% and apply for a refund after year-end using Form T634 (or an amended return). For a BC LP, the BC Ministry of Finance does not administer tax treaties; the Canada Revenue Agency is the sole competent authority. Under the Canada–US treaty, the US partner's share of business income is not taxable in Canada if the LP does not constitute a permanent establishment under Article V; income attributable to a fixed base of an individual is covered under Article XIV.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rate for royalties: 25% under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act on Canadian-source royalty payments (e.g., for the use of software, trademarks, or know-how) to non-residents; treaty rate for royalties under the Canada–US treaty is 0% for certain copyright royalties (including software) and 10% for patents and trademarks; under the Canada–OECD DTA model, most Canadian tax treaties reduce royalty withholding to 10% or less (often 0% for software copyright and cultural royalties).
